summary: Move the fused 29/110 reference from the translation to refs
rationale: The parsed translation ends with the closing quotation mark and “; 29/110”, while refs is empty. Remove that suffix from translation and set refs to the supplied reference object. summary: Restore corpus barqabal in place of maqqabāl
rationale: The cited verse 29/193 has “gḥəšwinalən barqabal d qarʕux”. The glossary instead substitutes maqqabāl, changing the initial consonants of the word. The supplied Ritter dictionary independently gives barqăbāl “Opfer, hingegeben”, agreeing with the context and translation “Opfergabe”. The correction retains the entry’s long ā convention.

summary: German contraction: in Sommer → im Sommer
rationale: The expression is “im Sommer”. The supplied edition translation at 8/10 reads “Ich fühlte mich wirklich im Sommer”.
The fixed expression is “Rücksicht darauf nehmen”. The corpus translation repeats the spelling error “rücksieht”; it does not justify the erroneous noun in the entry.

summary: German adjective ending: eines grünes Baumes → eines grünen Baumes
rationale: After “eines” the genitive singular adjective takes -en: “eines grünen Baumes”. The supplied corpus translation has the same grammatical slip; the correction is unambiguous German inflection.
In “so wäre ich nicht ...” the verb must be the past participle “herübergekommen”. “Herüberkommen” is the infinitive.

summary: Supply the missing English subject: (Perhaps) he is
rationale: The second sentence has no subject. Turoyo “hiye rab minan-yo” explicitly supplies hiye, “he”, and the edition translates “Vielleicht ist er Vornehmer als wir”.
The singular imperative is “Gib ihn her!”, corresponding to háw-li-yo. The supplied translation at 94/472 also reads “Gib ihn her!”.
The parenthetical German name corresponding to Mšiḥo is Christus; “Chritus” lacks s.
